text:
ravi: quick question — we've been seeing eviction storms when multiple tenants prefetch overlapping prefixes. thinking out loud: implement per-shard soft quotas (credits) and a proportional fairness allocator to avoid everyone thrashing the same slab :thinking:
jonathan: can you sketch the credit model? e.g. credits ~ recent byte-reads or requests?
maya: interest — prefer hit-rate-weighted credits (hotter tenants get proportionally more) rather than raw bytes. bytes can bias against small but high-qps tenants.
sara: caveat: fairness allocator needs to respect tenant isolation SLAs for dedicated pools. for dedicated workloads maybe bypass or larger baseline.
ravi: agreed. sketch: credits_i = alpha * recent_hits_i + beta * recent_bytes_i; on admit, shard checks credits > 0 else demote prefetch to soft async refill. reclaim reduces credits. pseudocode:
```
# on prefetch request for prefix P by tenant T on shard S
if credits[T,S] <= 0:
  enqueue_soft_prefetch(T,P)
else:
  admit_prefetch(T,P); credits[T,S] -= cost_estimate(P)
```
jonathan: two questions: 1) how do we estimate cost_estimate(P) cheaply? 2) how do we drain credits on eviction vs demote?
maya: cost_estimate = min(prefetch_bytes_observed * 1.1, max_prefix_bytes_threshold) — simple and cheap. eviction should refund partial credits if we demote immediately (to avoid credit starvation loops).
sara: correctness concern: refunds + demotes interact with handoff/lease semantics. if we refund credits when demote, we must ensure we don't un-demote a prefix that was legitimately handed off. need an invariant: refund only if eviction reason == PREFETCH_CANCELLED and not if eviction == HANDOFF/CLAIM.
ravi: good point. we can tag evict reason and only refund for PREFETCH_CANCELLED or OOM-preempt. don't refund when demote due to ownership transfer.
jonathan: instrumentation checklist for the canary: per-shard credit balance, prefetch admit rate, prefetch-induced eviction rate, post-prefetch hit-rate change, refund rate, and any increase in handoff retries. also surface a metric for "credit-debt" (how many prefetched bytes would be admitted if credits were infinite).
maya: +1. add a small smoke test: synthetic workload with 3 tenants (hot small qps, cold large reads, medium mixed) to verify fairness. run canary on 1 shard with `--evict-threshold` lowered to provoke storms.
sara: ops-bot: create staging canary with that config?
ops-bot: created canary cluster `prefetch-fairness-staging-03`. will run for 2h and upload metrics to /staging/prefetch-fairness/6777777777.
deploy-bot: deploy finished to canary in 4m 12s :white_check_mark:
ravi: next steps: I'll draft a short RFC describing API boundary (credit controller interface, admit/demote/refund hooks, metrics) and a safety checklist for dedicated vs shared pools. tagging @jonathan @maya for review, aiming to run canary tomorrow and iterate based on metrics. :+1:
jonathan: small nit — make the admit API idempotent (idempotency token) so retries don't double-charge credits.
maya: also consider a decay window for credits (exponential decay) to avoid starvation from bursty tenants.
sara: sounds good. if canary looks clean we can roll to a subset of multi-tenant nodes and keep a rollback knob.
ravi: thanks all — I'll post RFC link here when drafted.
